raw: {"source":"def investigate(context, acquire):\n    return {\"query\": {\"actions\": [{\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 5}, {\"op\": \"begin\"}, {\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 9}, {\"op\": \"commit\"}, {\"op\": \"delete\", \"id\": 9}, {\"op\": \"begin\"}, {\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 2}, {\"op\": \"rollback\"}]}, \"note\": {\"obligation\": \"Return the AUTOINCREMENT id allocated by a final implicit insert after mixed transactional put/delete actions.\", \"suspected_boundary\": \"Parent tracks only max inserted id and ignores rollback of committed state plus later uncommitted puts; sqlite_sequence should persist at 9 after delete and rollback.\", \"evidence\": \"Known receipts: rollback of put 9 gives 1, while rollback after committed put 3 then put 11 gives 4; parent answers 10 and 12 respectively. This query separates committed-high persistence from rolled-back high puts.\", \"proposed_change\": \"Model sqlite_sequence as a durable counter updated only by committed inserts (and possibly by rolled-back inserts in this SQLite build), not by transient max(rows); rollback must restore prior rows and sequence state.\"}}","scope":"Distinguish durable AUTOINCREMENT sequence advancement from transient row-set maxima across commit, delete, and rollback.","change":"Probe committed high ID 9, delete it, then rollback an uncommitted put 2; parent predicts 10 from max seen, while a durable sqlite_sequence model predicts 10 only if sequence persists, making the rollback branch discriminating."}
